### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/data.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/data.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **172** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `9a6fcdd25b080fdac8c640e5f03d04cbc8ade831` — the merge of head `12a6f2e15dd70fc9a938eeb0dbb23214ad043b6c` into base `4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 9a6fcdd25b080fdac8c640e5f03d04cbc8ade831 && git checkout 9a6fcdd25b080fdac8c640e5f03d04cbc8ade831
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a 12a6f2e15dd70fc9a938eeb0dbb23214ad043b6c && git checkout -B drift-repro 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a && git merge --no-ff 12a6f2e15dd70fc9a938eeb0dbb23214ad043b6c

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4bba8b8f02fdbdf30e9ad41fc5d2a6fdd3ccaf2a
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `12a6f2e15dd70fc9a938eeb0dbb23214ad043b6c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/data/managed-api-affordance.ts + none (no other file in the diff implements or enforces it; `.changeset/33522-retire-describe-managed-api-method-conflicts.md` is judged in ② for level, banner and ADR-0087 marker only; the test file and the two generated snapshots are the lane seat's ACCEPT, read here only to answer ①)

Inputs read: card #33522 body and all three comments (triage 6886170312, claim 6886195399, dev report 6887762168), PR #33583 body and file list (5 files), the net diff `origin/main...12a6f2e1` (merge base `8e63ed87`), and the 72 check-runs on the head: 57 success, 15 skipped, 0 failure, 0 pending (both `Check Changeset` runs completed success; `Lint & Repo Gates`, `Lint · CI, release & engine gates`, `TypeScript Type Check`, `Type Check UI`, `Test Core` 8/8, `Test UI` 16/16, `Build Core`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `Dogfood Regression Gate` all success). Read outside the diff, not reviewed: `scripts/check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` and `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` on `main`, AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3, `packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `packages/lint/src/validate-managed-api-methods.ts`, `packages/spec/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Public surface: one published runtime export removed from `@objectstack/spec/data`. Right, and declared as what it is (a narrowing).** `describeManagedApiMethodConflicts` reached the package's public entries through exactly one path: `packages/spec/src/data/index.ts:192` (`export * from './managed-api-affordance'`). The root entry `packages/spec/src/index.ts` exports no domain namespace (its header says so, and its only star exports are `./stack.zod` and `./conversions/index.js`); on `main` the name occurs in `api-surface/data.json` and `export-origins/data.json` and in no other snapshot (`root.json` and the 17 other subpath snapshots: 0 hits). So the removal is from the `./data` subpath alone, as the changeset says.
- **Nothing else reachable is lost. Right.** The diff deletes one function and its docblock (22 lines) and no type, constant or re-export. `ManagedApiMethodConflict` (its parameter type), `MANAGED_WRITE_VERB_AFFORDANCE` and `checkManagedApiMethodAffordances` are still declared and still present in both snapshots at the head (`export-origins/data.json` lines 443, 450, 894). The function's return type was `string`; no named type existed only for it.
- **Generated snapshots: exactly one removed name each. Right.** `api-surface/data.json` loses the line `describeManagedApiMethodConflicts (function)`; `export-origins/data.json` loses the one key mapping it to `src/data/managed-api-affordance.ts`. No other line moves in either file, and `git grep` at the head finds the name in no snapshot.
- **Accept-set: unchanged. Right.** No schema, no authorable key, no verdict moves. `checkManagedApiMethodAffordances` is byte-identical, so every finding of `object/managed-api-method-unaffordable` and every boot-time strip is what it was.
- **Test surface: the removed function's own `describe` block (4 cases) and its import go; nothing else. Right.** The remaining suites still use `managed()`, `verbs()` and the `ManagedApiMethodConflict` type import, so no orphan is left behind (`Type Check · source gates` and `Lint · ESLint` success on the head).

### ② Semver level

- **Level `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`: right.** AGENTS.md step 3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol:` kind alone, `none` takes `patch`, and "a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition". A removed runtime function is not something a metadata author can write.
- **`Metadata-protocol: none`: right.** No key, accepted value, metadata type, default or meaning changes. Line-initial in both the changeset body and the PR body.
- **`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`: right.** The published surface shrinks by one export and no rule or schema clause is added; `(narrowing)` is the BREAKING arm and the body carries the `**BREAKING**` banner, the bang in the subject, and the consumer named (a TypeScript caller importing the name from `@objectstack/spec/data`). Line-initial in both bodies, and the two bodies agree.
- **The caller's fix is in the body: sufficient.** Step 3 asks a removed export to carry its FROM to TO mapping and one-line fix. The body states the compiler error (`TS2305`), the action (delete the import) and the replacement (word the message from each conflict's `verb` and `needs`). There is no TO symbol to map to; the sentence is the whole migration. It is written as prose, not a FROM/TO block, which is forced by the marker below.
- **ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`: honest and sufficient on `main` today. Not a must-fix.** Read against the gate source and the ADR on `main`:
  - `runtime-export-retired` is the category built for this class (ADR-0087 D9), and it is closed to this operand by the gate's own text: "A subpath entry (`@scope/pkg/sub`). Only the root entry is read; a retirement from a subpath names no operand this category can verify, so it is refused at the mapping step rather than assumed." The ADR's D9 says the same under "What this does not decide". With the root-package operand, predicate 1 `retired-from-entry` reads `packages/spec/src/index.ts` at the merge base and the name is not among its exports (confirmed in ① from `root.json` and the entry source), so the claim would be false, not merely unverifiable. Claiming it would be the dishonest marker.
  - The other fact-backed categories are closed on facts the tree confirms: the package publishes (`unpublished` false); the diff adds no ledger entry and none exists for a function (`registered`, `already-registered`); a function is neither an exported type declaration at HEAD nor a type narrowed off `any` (`runtime-interface-only`, `type-surface-only`).
  - `no-migration-prescription` has two refusals on `main`: a body carrying a prescription the detector reads, and a changeset declaring `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`. Neither applies: the kind is `none` (which the ADR says "keep[s] the exemption"), and the gate's check-run is green on this head. The category's substantive claim, that the ledger and `objectstack migrate meta` have nothing to rewrite, is true here; D8 names this exact case ("it simply cannot tell a prescription for a metadata upgrader from a prescription for a source-code consumer, and only the first is the ledger's business").
  - The marker's justification states the limitation in the open (the name lives on `./data`, the category reads the root only). It is not held by a concealed detector miss: nothing in the body is an arrowless FROM/TO line of the kind D9 was written to stop.
- **nit (N1, accepted deviation, no fix owed):** the caller's fix is a sentence because this category refuses a FROM/TO block; the ideal shape is `runtime-export-retired @objectstack/spec/data#describeManagedApiMethodConflicts` with a FROM line, which only PR #33520's gate can verify. No effect on correctness or on what an upgrading consumer reads.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (marker now vs. hold behind PR #33520): answered, option A. Land as is.** #33520 is open, unmerged and awaiting its own tier's record; `main`'s gate is the contract in force, and under it this marker is the one true disposition (②). Holding a p3 dead-surface removal behind a Tier H PR to swap one marker for another that says the same thing to the same reader buys nothing. After merge nothing is owed either: the ADR states a changeset already breaking at the branch point "is inherited and never re-judged", so #33520 landing later does not re-grade this one. If #33520 lands first, the swap is optional and is a changeset-only (prose face) edit; it moves the head, so it would need this record re-pointed. Not escalated.
- **out_of_scope: `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md` (two released entries) names "the spec's `describeManagedApiMethodConflicts` sentence". Answered: correct to leave.** Release-owned (AGENTS.md: never edited in a code PR), and the sentence is history that is true of its release ("no longer appends ...").
- **Reviewer-raised, outside this diff, no action here:** the registry's boot warning (`packages/objectql/src/registry.ts`, `reconcileManagedApiMethods`) and the lint rule's message and hint still name `userActions` as the remedy on every bucket. That is the defect PR #33517 (card #32134) owns by ruling; this PR neither touches nor worsens it. The changeset's sentence that those two "each word their own message" is true as written and makes no claim that their wording is right on `synced`.
- **Residual, stated by the dev and confirmed as stated:** the cloud repository cannot be read from here and the org code search only covers what the token can see. A cloud import would fail at compile time (`TS2305`) on upgrade, never silently. Accepted under the claim's route ruling; not escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

`packages/spec/src/data/managed-api-affordance.ts`: **the retirement holds.** No must-fix, no should-fix.

- **Zero consumers, re-verified at the head.** `git grep describeManagedApiMethodConflicts` over the whole tree at `12a6f2e1` (including `ui/`, `examples/`, `content/`, `docs/`, `skills/`): the changeset (3 lines) and `packages/lint/CHANGELOG.md` (2 released entries, prose). No source, test, doc, skill or snapshot. On `main` the only additional hits are the definition, its own test and the two snapshots. `/home/user/hotcrm` and `/home/user/gallery`: 0 hits in the working tree and on `origin/main`. Org code search `describeManagedApiMethodConflicts org:objectstack-ai`: 4 hits, all in objectstack (definition, test, the two snapshots; the index still reflects `main`). A partial-name sweep (`describeManagedApi`) finds nothing a string-built or renamed reference could hide behind.
- **Attempt to break it: a caller that relied on the sentence.** The two production callers of the predicate build their own text and do not import the helper: `reconcileManagedApiMethods` (`registry.ts`) composes its warning from each conflict's `verb`, and `validateManagedApiMethods` composes `message` and `hint` from `verb` and `needs`. Removing the helper changes no string either emits. `Test Core` 8/8 and `Test UI` 16/16 are green with it gone.
- **Attempt to break it: a comment left false.** The only prose that said "the one sentence both consumers say" was the removed function's own docblock, and it leaves with the function. It was already false on `main` (neither consumer called it), so the removal makes the file truer, not staler. Every remaining comment was read against the tree: the file header's "exactly two consumers" describes the predicate and names `reconcileManagedApiMethods` and `validateManagedApiMethods`, both of which call `checkManagedApiMethodAffordances` at the head; "ONE table, read by the boot-time strip and by the authoring-time gate" is true; the docblocks of `MANAGED_WRITE_VERB_AFFORDANCE`, `ManagedApiMethodConflict` and `checkManagedApiMethodAffordances` name nothing removed. In the callers, `registry.ts` ("The judgement itself is NOT here ...") and the header of `validate-managed-api-methods.ts` ("All judgement lives in the SHARED predicate") speak of the predicate only; neither claims a shared sentence. The test file's header ("These cases mirror `reconcileManagedApiMethods`'s own suite") stays true of what remains.
- **Attempt to break it: the alternative route.** The card offered "align" only if a consumer exists. None does, and the helper cannot be made true without widening its signature: `ManagedApiMethodConflict` carries `verb`, `needs`, `index` and no bucket, so it cannot know a `synced` object refuses the `userActions` remedy (ADR-0153 D4; `object.zod.ts` line 4598). Keeping a published sentence that is wrong on one bucket and read by nobody is the worse of the two outcomes; retire is the right route, and it matches the claim's ruling.
- **Changeset prose against the tree.** Each factual sentence checks: the subpath, the absence of callers, the two consumers wording their own messages, the three symbols that stay, the `synced` refusal. No overclaim found.

Findings: N1 (nit, ②, accepted deviation). No must-fix, no should-fix; nits alone end the round.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-8c9p9x`
Reviewed-by: `session_01FEkQ5mecqk8M5q9vjKj6aS`

**VERDICT: PASS**
